note.text:
Phones: a mobile phone (cell phone) can call, send text messages, take photos and use the internet; a landline stays in one place. People choose a phone for its price, battery, camera and memory.
Telephone language:
• Answer: “Hello, Mount Fako Clinic. How can I help you?”
• Say who you are: “This is Ebai.” (not “I am Ebai” or “Here is Ebai”)
• Ask for someone: “May I speak to Nurse Manyi, please?”
• Wait: “Hold on, please.” / “Please hold.”
• Messages: “Can I take a message?” “Could you tell her …?”
• Mistakes: “Sorry, you have the wrong number.”
• End: “I'll call back later. Goodbye.”
On the phone, speak clearly and politely, and do not shout.

worked_example.problem: {n} calls {p}'s office, but {p} is out. Write what {n} and the secretary say.
steps: The secretary answers: “Good morning, Fon and Sons. How can I help you?”
{n} says who he is and asks: “This is {n}. May I speak to {p}, please?”
The secretary offers a message: “I'm sorry, he's out. Can I take a message?” — “Yes, please. Could you tell him I called?”
worked_example.answer: “This is {n}. May I speak to {p}, please?” — “I'm sorry, he's out. Can I take a message?”

cards.idea: Read this telephone call. (In class you would listen to it.)
example: Receptionist: Good afternoon, Mount Fako Clinic. How can I help you?
Ebai: Good afternoon. May I speak to Nurse Manyi, please?
Receptionist: Hold on, please … I'm sorry, she's busy at the moment. Can I take a message?
Ebai: Yes, please. This is Ebai Tanyi. Could you tell her I can't come on Friday? I'll call back tomorrow.
Receptionist: Certainly. I'll give her the message. Goodbye.
